options.content:
# Institution Activity

Overall activity at <institution> between <start date> and <end date>.

Computing is a major contributor to energy consumption, and thus is one of the main sources of the carbon emission of our research. In the
context of the global climate crisis, it is imperative that individuals and organizations find ways to assess then reduce the carbon footprint of their
work.
This page aims to represent the carbon footprint that we are, collectively and individually, responsible for at <institution>.
 SLURM jobs
submitted to High Performance Clusters are logged automatically (including information such as resource requested, run time, memory
efficiency, etc.), and the corresponding carbon footprint was calculated using the framework proposed by [Green Algorithms](https://www.green-algorithms.org) and the following assumptions:

|Type|Value|
|----|-----|
|CPU |5.9 - 9.4 W/core|
|GPU |NVIDIA A100 (300 W) and NVIDIA Tesla P100 (250 W)|
|Memory power | 0.3725 W/GB|
|Power usage effectiveness| 1.15|
|Carbon intensity |231.12 gCO<sub>2</sub> e/kWh|
|Energy cost| £0.34/kWh|

----
We built this tool in the hope to raise awareness of computing usage, highlight resources waste, and foster good computing practices. This
is intended to be a lightweight carbon footprint calculator, not a cluster monitoring system.
----

# Departments

Carbon footprint of all departments between <start date> and <end date>.

panels.description: Carbon footprint of all departments between <start date> and <end-date>

targets.rawSql: SELECT department, SUM(carbonfootprint) FROM (select u.user_name, u.department, d.carbonfootprint from ga_user u INNER JOIN ga_data_aggregate d on u.user_name = d.user_name) GROUP BY department ORDER BY SUM(carbonfootprint) DESC;

panels.title: Main contributors to the total carbon footprint

targets.rawSql:
SELECT submitdate, SUM(carbonfootprint) AS "CFP", department 
FROM
	(SELECT d.submitdate, u.department, d.carbonfootprint 
	FROM
	ga_user u INNER JOIN ga_data_aggregate d ON u.user_name = d.user_name)
GROUP BY
submitdate, department;

SELECT department AS "Department", to_char(SUM(carbonfootprint)/1000, '99999') AS "Carbon footprint (kgCO2e)", to_char(SUM(cost), '99999.99') as "Cost(£)" FROM (select u.user_name, u.department, d.carbonfootprint, d.cost from ga_user u INNER JOIN ga_data_aggregate d on u.user_name = d.user_name) GROUP BY department ORDER BY department ASC;

options.content:
# Efficiency metrics
## Failed jobs
Because any resource spent on a job is wasted if the job fails, it is important to test scripts and pipelines on small datasets. The chart below
shows the daily success and failure rates of jobs that completed in the period.

targets.rawSql: SELECT SUM(n_jobs) AS "No. of jobs completed", to_char(SUM(carbonfootprint_failedjobs),'99999999.99') AS "Failed jobs' footprint (kgCO2e)", to_char(SUM(cost_failedjobs), '9999999') AS "Cost (£) of failed jobs", to_char((SUM(n_jobs-n_success)::float/SUM(n_jobs))*100, '999.99') AS "% of failed jobs" FROM ga_data_aggregate;

SELECT submitdate, (SUM(n_jobs-n_success)::float/SUM(n_jobs))*100 AS "Failed jobs",  (SUM(n_success)::float/SUM(n_jobs))*100 AS "Successful jobs" FROM ga_data_aggregate GROUP BY submitdate ORDER BY submitdate;
SELECT SUM(n_jobs-n_success) AS "Failed jobs", SUM(n_success) AS "Successful jobs" FROM ga_data_aggregate ORDER BY SUM(n_jobs-n_success) ASC ;

panels.title: Distribution of failed and successful jobs.

options.content:
# Memory efficiency (all institution)

Memory can be a significant source of waste, because the power draw from memory mainly depends on the memory available, not on the actual
memory used. The chart below shows the distribution of the memory efficiency collected from all jobs in the period chosen (the closer to 100% the better).

targets.rawSql:
SELECT r.range as "Memory efficiency (%)", SUM(n_jobs) as "Number of jobs"
from 
(
    select '0-4' as range, 4 as endrange
        union all select '5-9', 9
        union all select '10-14', 14
        union all select '15-19', 19
        union all select '20-24', 24
        union all select '25-29', 29
        union all select '30-34', 34
        union all select '35-39', 39
        union all select '40-44', 44
        union all select '45-49', 49
        union all select '50-54', 54
        union all select '55-59', 59
        union all select '60-64', 64
        union all select '65-69', 69
        union all select '70-74', 74
        union all select '75-79', 79
        union all select '80-84', 84
        union all select '85-89', 89
        union all select '90-94', 94
        union all select '95-99', 99
        union all select '100', 100
) as r
left join ga_data_aggregate on 
r.endrange = case 
    when ROUND((1/memoryoverallocationfactor)*100) = 100 then 100
    when ROUND((1/memoryoverallocationfactor)*100) > 95 then 99
    when ROUND((1/memoryoverallocationfactor)*100) > 90 then 94
    when ROUND((1/memoryoverallocationfactor)*100) > 85 then 89
    when ROUND((1/memoryoverallocationfactor)*100) > 80 then 84
    when ROUND((1/memoryoverallocationfactor)*100) > 75 then 79
    when ROUND((1/memoryoverallocationfactor)*100) > 70 then 74
    when ROUND((1/memoryoverallocationfactor)*100) > 65 then 69
    when ROUND((1/memoryoverallocationfactor)*100) > 60 then 64
    when ROUND((1/memoryoverallocationfactor)*100) > 55 then 59
    when ROUND((1/memoryoverallocationfactor)*100) > 50 then 54
    when ROUND((1/memoryoverallocationfactor)*100) > 45 then 49
    when ROUND((1/memoryoverallocationfactor)*100) > 40 then 44
    when ROUND((1/memoryoverallocationfactor)*100) > 35 then 39
    when ROUND((1/memoryoverallocationfactor)*100) > 30 then 34
    when ROUND((1/memoryoverallocationfactor)*100) > 25 then 29
    when ROUND((1/memoryoverallocationfactor)*100) > 20 then 24
    when ROUND((1/memoryoverallocationfactor)*100) > 15 then 19
    when ROUND((1/memoryoverallocationfactor)*100) > 10 then 14
    when ROUND((1/memoryoverallocationfactor)*100) > 5 then 9
    when ROUND((1/memoryoverallocationfactor)*100) >= 0 then 4
    end
    --WHERE user_name='${__user.login}'
    group by r.range, r.endrange order by r.endrange;
SELECT MIN(submitdate) AS "Start of submitdate period", MAX(submitdate) AS "End of submitdate period", SUM(n_jobs) AS "Number of jobs" from ga_data_aggregate ;
